reason: Both conversations get the key safety steps right: they tell her not to touch the plug or machine, to get off the wet floor, and to isolate power at the dry consumer unit. Conversation 2 is more forceful and actionable, saying 'You must switch off the power at your consumer unit right now' and addressing the machine still running. It also asks useful diagnostic questions and warns against moving the machine or checking behind it. Its weaknesses are that it guesses the inlet valve or an internal hose without evidence (the real cause is the door seal), and it stays vague about turning off the water. Conversation 1 never explicitly instructs her to go and switch off at the consumer unit in its second reply, and it lists leak causes that don't fit the front leak, so it is less actionable.
